payload.rationale: The supplied Freddie Mac observations place the September 17 rate at 6.95%, following weekly increases of 1, 5, 5, and 19 basis points. At the usual two-decimal publication precision, YES requires September 24's first published value to be at least 7.02%, a further increase of 7 basis points. That is plausible given the recent upward movement, but the latest large increase is not sufficient evidence that another substantial rise will follow. I assign 45%, allowing for some continuation while placing substantial weight on stabilization or reversal. This is a judgmental forecast, not a probability fitted to the five observations. The strongest reason the estimate could be too low is that the recent acceleration reflects a persistent repricing that continues into the September 17–23 measurement window. The strongest reason it could be too high is that the 19-basis-point increase was a temporary jump that has already fully entered the survey, leaving the next reading flat or lower. Settlement depends on the specified first-published Freddie Mac national average, not a daily lender quote or subsequent revision.
limitations: Only five recent weekly observations are supplied; they do not establish a reliable transition distribution.
No contemporaneous Treasury yields, mortgage-backed-security pricing, lender quotes, or within-week rate observations are available.
Continuation and reversal assumptions rely on general rate behavior, not independently verified September 2026 market developments.
